stimuli.description: Immersive Virtual Environments (IVEs) of university classrooms with three different illuminance levels (100 lx, 300 lx, 500 lx). The virtual classroom was windowless, measured 16.50 × 8.50 m, and simulated tubular lamps fitted into 56 cm × 56 cm luminaires (45 lamps total). Renderings were 360° panoramas displayed via HTC Vive HMD.

tables.description: Statistical treatments for each phase of the study, including data used and expected results.
Mean and standard deviation of sense of presence for each item of the SUS questionnaire across three illuminance levels (100 lx, 300 lx, 500 lx).

limitations: Time of day was not controlled due to sample size constraints.
Only illuminance level was varied; other lighting variables (e.g., uniformity, colour temperature) were kept constant.
Only one classroom design was used; different classroom designs might produce different effects.
VR might induce students to focus more on enjoying the experience than on task performance, requiring future protocols to ensure full task involvement.
The presence of other students and different viewpoint positions within the classroom were excluded due to parameterization difficulties, potentially influencing task performance.
